transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this meeting because we have one mobile bariatric lift available for immediate assignment, and both the North and South inpatient units have patients whose transfer plans are being reviewed for use of the lift. Before I can finalize the assignment, hospital policy requires me to hold a brief equipment-readiness check with physical therapy, facilities, nursing education, and infection prevention. I'd like to go through that check now so we can make a timely decision. Could each of you provide a quick status update on your area's readiness?

transcript.text: From a physical therapy perspective, I want to share my assessment findings for both patients. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. Based on these clinical assessments, the South unit patient has the greater need for the bariatric lift.

transcript.text: From a facilities perspective, I need to share an important equipment constraint. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. Additionally, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. So from a facilities standpoint, the lift can only be safely deployed to the South unit.

Three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation, and hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer. Their available coverage is 07:00-19:00 daily.
